entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jaya Harivarman I, also known as Sivänandana, was the Phan Rang noble king of Champa from around 1125 to 1145 CE. Rising to power during the Khmer-Cham wars, he consolidated his control over Champa and established a strong, centralized state. His rule was marked by a series of military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, including the Khmer Empire and the Champa's own rival nobles.




 Jaya Harivarman I's legacy can be seen in the continued stability and prosperity of Champa during his reign, as well as the lasting impact of his military campaigns on the region's politics and geography. His successors, including his son Jaya Harivarman II, continued to build on his achievements, further solidifying Champa's position as a major power in Southeast Asia.





 The most striking testament to Jaya Harivarman I's significance lies in the enduring legacy of his dynasty, which continued to shape Champa's history for centuries to come. Despite the eventual decline and fall of Champa, Jaya Harivarman I's name remains synonymous with bravery, strategic brilliance, and the indomitable will to power in the face of overwhelming odds.
